- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if price drops 2–3% from recent high, forecast should not drop below 1% below prior low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
